works.title: Vacuum-Assisted Assembly of GO/MXene Lamellae for Enhanced PES Nanofiltration Performance
institutions: Wuhan University of Science and Technology
Hubei Key Laboratory for Efficient Utilization and Agglomeration of Metallurgic Mineral Resources, Wuhan University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China.
College of Resource and Environmental Engineering, Wuhan University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China.
works.abstract: Polyethersulfone (PES) membranes suffer from intrinsic hydrophobicity and severe fouling, limiting their applicability in dye-containing wastewater treatment. In this study, thin-film composite PES/GO/MXene nanofiltration (NF) membranes were fabricated through a vacuum-assisted nano-intercalation strategy that enables controlled assembly of GO and MXene nanosheets on PES substrates. Systematic tuning of the GO-to-MXene ratio revealed clear correlations between lamellar structure, surface chemistry and the resulting water permeability, dye rejection, and antifouling behavior. The optimized membrane (GO:MXene = 1:2) achieved a high pure water permeance of 50.1 L·m −2 ·h −1 ·bar −1 together with rejection rates of 97.3% for methylene blue and 93.8% for rhodamine B. Moreover, the membrane demonstrated stable dye rejection and a flux recovery ratio of ∼84% over five bovine serum albumin fouling-cleaning cycles, demonstrating good short-term operational stability. This work provides a promising interfacial engineering strategy to incorporate mixed 2D lamellar nanochannels into polymeric NF membranes for efficient purification of dye-contaminated wastewater.

works.title: Evolution of smart nanofiltration membranes: from traditional modification to intelligent precise filtration
works.abstract: As a novel class of functional separation media, smart nanofiltration (NF) membranes are capable of dynamically regulating separation performance upon external environmental stimuli, enabling intelligent and precise filtration with high efficiency. Unlike traditional static NF membranes with fixed, unadjustable separation capacity, such smart membranes offer unique advantages in tunability. Faced with global water scarcity and the growing pressure of industrial wastewater remediation, research communities across the globe have significantly expanded research and development investment in smart NF membranes in recent years. This review systematically summarizes mainstream modification strategies of smart NF membranes, typical stimuli-responsive categories, as well as their practical engineering applications. Five dominant modification techniques, including surface grafting, interfacial polymerization, blending modification, surface coating, and layer-by-layer self-assembly are elaborated, with their respective advantages and drawbacks in practical industrial scenarios comprehensively summarized. In terms of responsive behaviors, five mainstream stimuli-responsive modes are illustrated, along with representative membrane materials corresponding to each responsive type. The state-of-the-art applications and inherent bottlenecks of stimuli-responsive NF membranes are thoroughly discussed. In addition, the emerging multi-stimuli response and its existing application scenarios are also introduced. Finally, this work identifies critical bottlenecks restricting the further industrial translation of smart NF membranes and proposes targeted optimization strategies. We anticipate that smart NF membranes will provide viable solutions to diverse water pollution challenges and deliver prominent advances in resource recovery, precise ion separation, and sustainable industrial circulation in future practical processes.

works.title: Ordered MoS2 Nanochannels Regulated by CNT for Conformation-Dependent Sieving in High-Salinity Organic Wastewater
works.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of the pharmaceutical and fine chemical industries has escalated the discharge of high-salinity organic wastewater, which contains complex solutes and biotoxic antibiotics that are difficult to treat conventionally due to their high osmotic pressure and environmental persistence. Here, we developed a high-performance composite nanofiltration membrane by incorporating hydroxylated single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT-OH) into electrochemically exfoliated monolayer MoS2 nanosheets. SWCNT-OH acts as a structural regulator, preventing MoS2 restacking and constructing stable, highly ordered 1.5 nm interlayer channels. At an optimized mass ratio of 6:1, the membrane achieves a water permeance of 28.0 L·m–2·h–1·bar–1 and a separation factor of 59.8 for oxytetracycline (OTC)/NaCl mixtures. Notably, rejection is governed by the molecular projected cross-sectional dimension relative to the 1.5 nm channels, demonstrating a conformation-dependent selectivity. These results highlight MoS2/CNT membranes as a durable solution for sustainable industrial wastewater treatment.

works.title: Polyethylene Glycol‐Regulated Finger‐Sponge Substrate Enabling High‐Performance Nanofiltration Membranes for Efficient Mg <sup>2+</sup> /Li <sup>+</sup> Separation
institutions: East China University of Science and Technology
School of Materials Science and Engineering East China University of Science and Technology Shanghai China
National Collaborative Innovation Center for Salt Lake Resources Chemistry and Process Engineering, School of Chemical Engineering Qinghai University Xining China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient lithium recovery from salt‐lake brines relies on the precise discrimination and lithium ions separation from magnesium ions. In this study, polyethersulfone (PES) ultrafiltration (UF) substrate layer featuring finger‐like and optimized finger‐sponge transitional structures were fabricated by varying polyethylene glycol (PEG) concentrations via phase inversion. These substrate layers served as platforms for the growth of polyamide (PA) active layers through interfacial polymerization (IP). The performance of the synthesized nanofiltration (NF) membranes was assessed via the fractionation of Mg 2+ and Li + from high Mg/Li ratio brines. These results indicate the substrate layer with a finger‐sponge transitional structure exhibits higher surface hydrophilicity. The PA NF membranes constructed on this substrate layer exhibit significantly enhanced divalent cations (Mg 2+ ) rejection, while maintaining effective Mg 2+ /Li + separation performance under high Mg/Li ratio and high salinity conditions. When the Mg/Li ratio of the feed solution is 20:1, the PA NF membrane achieves 99.6% ± 0.1% rejection of divalent cation Mg 2+ , with an Mg/Li separation factor (SF) of up to 50 ± 7. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that optimizing substrate layer transitions is an effective approach yet previously overlooked to fine‐tune PA layer properties, thereby significantly advancing the Mg 2+ /Li + separation performance of PA NF membranes.

works.title: Interplay between silicon quantum dot surface functionality and diisocyanate chemistry in polyurea thin-film nanocomposite nanofiltration membranes for dye/salt separation
works.abstract: Dye/salt separation requires nanofiltration membranes that retain organic dyes while allowing dissolved salts to pass. This study examined how silicon quantum dot (SiQD) surface functionality and organic diisocyanate chemistry affect polyurea thin-film nanocomposite membranes prepared by interfacial polymerization. Three diamine-functionalized SiQDs were combined with three organic diisocyanates to compare their effects on membrane properties and separation performance. Among the investigated combinations, the membrane prepared with m -phenylenediamine (MPDA)-functionalized SiQDs and 1,3-bis(isocyanatomethyl)cyclohexane (BIMC) showed the best overall dye/salt separation performance. Under the determined fabrication conditions, the MPDASiQDs–BIMC/polysulfone membrane had a pure-water flux of 39.11 ± 4.47 LMH and rejected 98.24 ± 0.46% Rose Bengal, 97.93 ± 0.68% Methyl Blue, and 96.11 ± 0.91% Congo Red, while Na₂SO₄ and NaCl rejections were 27.92 ± 2.37% and 8.69 ± 1.83%, respectively. For the Rose Bengal/NaCl feed, the membrane rejected 97.84% of Rose Bengal and 5.83% of NaCl. For the Rose Bengal/Na₂SO₄ feed, it rejected 97.70% of Rose Bengal and 17.84% of Na₂SO₄. Rose Bengal rejection also remained above 96% across feed concentrations of 10–600 mg L −1 , although flux decreased at higher concentrations. During continuous filtration for approximately 168 h, dye rejection remained above 90%, while flux gradually decreased to approximately 80% of its initial value. These results show that SiQD surface functionality and diisocyanate chemistry can be varied to obtain polyurea–SiQD membranes that retain dyes while allowing salts to pass.

works.title: Recent progress in polycrystalline metal-organic framework membranes for liquid phase separation
works.abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF)-based membranes have attracted considerable attention for liquid separation applications due to their intrinsic porosity, tunable pore structures, and structural diversity, which enable precise and efficient separation of complex liquid mixtures in both aqueous and organic systems. Among various types of MOF membranes, polycrystalline MOF membranes, characterized by high crystallinity and well-defined reticular pore networks, show strong potential for solvent resistance and liquid-phase separation applications. This review summarizes recent advances in fabricating polycrystalline membranes using diverse synthesis and assembly strategies. It discusses the applications of these membranes in liquid-phase separation technologies, particularly nanofiltration (NF), pervaporation (PV), forward osmosis (FO), and chiral separation. Finally, it discusses strategies for large-scale fabrication and mechanical reinforcement of polycrystalline MOF membranes, emphasizing rational materials design and membrane engineering to accelerate their transition to practical, industrial implementation.

works.title: Lamellar Cristae‐Mimetic Sieving Membranes for Petrochemical Refining
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Catalysis Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics Chinese Academy of Sciences Dalian P. R. China
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing P. R. China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Isomerization processes produce approximately four million barrels of gasoline per day worldwide. Membrane‐based extraction of low‐concentration linear alkane residues from isomerate can improves both process economics and fuel octane number. However, this separation remains constrained by the permeance‐selectivity trade‐off. Here, by exploiting lattice‐mismatch strain during structural transformation, we engineered metal–organic framework nanosheet membranes that bend to a minimal curvature radius of 98.7 nm, forming a lamellar cristae‐mimetic architecture with a large surface area. An ultrathin sieving layer was continuously integrated onto this structure, delivering a 3‐fold increase in linear‐alkane permeance together with higher selectivity than conventional flat membranes. As a result, the octane number of isomerate increased from 70.6 to 92.6 over an equivalent duration of 2.45 h kmol −1 m −2 . This work presents a promising strategy for highly efficient petrochemical refining.

works.title: Positively Charged Hollow Fiber Nanofiltration Membrane With an <scp>SPSf</scp> / <scp>PEI</scp> Bilayer Prepared via Dip‐Coating
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials School of Materials Science and Engineering, Tiangong University Tianjin People's Republic of China

Liaoning Key Laboratory of Chemical Additive Synthesis and Separation, Panjin Key Laboratory of Membrane Science and Process Engineering, Panjin Institute of Industrial Technology Dalian University of Technology Panjin Liaoning China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofiltration (NF) has attracted considerable interest in water purification and resource recovery. Hollow fiber membranes offer high packing density, large surface‐area‐to‐volume ratio, and low‐pressure high‐flux operation. However, the fabrication of hollow fiber NF membranes often suffers from non‐uniform and discontinuous separation layers, while most conventional NF membranes are negatively charged and inclined to fouling caused by the adsorption of positively charged ions. In this work, a positively charged hollow fiber NF membrane was fabricated by constructing a sulfonated polysulfone (SPSf)/polyethyleneimine (PEI) electrostatic assembly bilayer via dip‐coating. The SPSf interlayer was first coated onto the polyethersulfone (PES) surface to enhance interfacial adhesion, facilitate PEI assembly, and prevent excessive PEI penetration into the membrane pores, thereby forming a dense, defect‐free selective layer via electrostatic interactions. The PES/SPSf‐PEI membrane showed high rejection for MgCl 2 (90.96%), crystal violet (99.56%), and rhodamine B (99.81%). Moreover, a flux recovery ratio of 86.77% was achieved after three fouling‐cleaning cycles using rhodamine B as a model foulant. This work provides a facile and controllable approach for preparing high‐performance positively charged hollow fiber NF membranes, showing great potential for divalent cation rejection and dye treatment.

works.title: Membrane-driven and hybrid pathways for magnesium recovery from aqueous brines and industrial wastewater: a review
works.abstract: Magnesium is a critical raw material with growing industrial demand, yet vast and largely untapped reservoirs exist in desalination reject brines, saltwork bitterns, hypersaline lake brines, and industrial wastewaters. Magnesium recovery from these streams is attracting increasing attention as a strategy to reduce brine disposal, mitigate salinity-management challenges, and decrease reliance on energy-intensive primary production. This review critically evaluates membrane-based and membrane-enabled hybrid routes for magnesium recovery, with conventional methods introduced briefly as a performance baseline. Membrane technologies covered include nanofiltration, forward osmosis, electrodialysis, membrane distillation, and ion-exchange membrane electrolysis, as well as hybrid flowsheets integrating precipitation and crystallization. Key findings indicate that nanofiltration is often the most cost-effective option, reporting Mg rejection above 90% and operating costs as low as ~0.10 USD per m 3 of treated stream. Electro-membrane systems provide strong ionic control but are frequently constrained by scaling, fouling, and case-dependent economics. Membrane-enabled hybrids can achieve magnesium purities above 98% and recoveries approaching 99.9% under optimized conditions, yet many studies remain proof-of-concept and lack long-duration validation and harmonized reporting of energy and cost. The review identifies key gaps and provides decision-relevant guidance for scalable, circular magnesium recovery.

works.title: Influence of pressure on the separation of L-citrulline from watermelon rind juice by nanofiltration
works.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of extracting L-citrulline from watermelon rind juice using nanofiltration under varying operating pressures from 10 to 40 bar. A nanofiltration membrane DK2540F30 with an active filtration area of 2.6 m² and a fully recirculating feed mode was utilized. The effect of pressure was discovered by monitoring the permeate fluxes of pretreated watermelon rind juice in comparison to that of pure water. Simultaneously, the selective separation of L-citrulline and D-glucose in the permeate was also investigated. The permeate flux of pure water demonstrated a linear correlation with the applied pressure within the range of 10 to 40 bar, whereas the flux behavior of the pretreated watermelon rind juice displayed a non-linear response under the same conditions. The optimal operating pressure was determined to be 35 bar, at which the membrane flux achieved its peak value of 30.00 L.m- ².h - ¹, and a significant rejection rate between L-citrulline (-172.26%) and D-glucose (48.43%) was observed. Membrane fouling was also found at this particular pressure as indicated by a pronounced reduction in permeate flux within the first 5 min, followed by a gradual and sustained decline over time. This reduction was mainly associated with a pronounced rise in fouling resistance, which nearly doubled within the first 9 min and was followed by a gradual increase until the 12-minute mark. A pronounced disparity in rejection rates was observed between Lcitrulline (-172.26%) and D-glucose (48.43%). These findings highlight the capability of nanofiltration as an innovative separation approach for the efficient extraction of Lcitrulline from watermelon rind juice.

works.title: Mechanistic insights into ultrafiltration fouling mitigation by coagulation pretreatment in livestock biogas slurry treatment
institutions: Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography
State Key Laboratory of Desert and Oasis Ecology
works.abstract: The treatment and utilization of livestock biogas slurry (BS) is significantly hindered by severe membrane fouling associated with high turbidity and complex dissolved organic matter (DOM). This study established an integrated coagulation-ultrafiltration (UF) pretreatment system using aluminum sulfate or ferric chloride as coagulants to provide stable influent for subsequent membrane concentration. Results demonstrated that while raw BS caused a rapid increase in transmembrane pressure (TMP) during UF, optimized coagulation at 3 g/L maintained TMP below 10 kPa over 6 h. Specifically, reversible resistance ( R re ) decreased by 92.9–99.0%, and irreversible resistance ( R ir ) decreased by 65.9–79.0%. Particle-related characteristics were closely associated with R re , whereas R ir was governed by multiple interacting factors. Mechanistically, interfacial thermodynamic analysis revealed that optimized coagulation increased the interaction free energies for both membrane-foulant adhesion and foulant-foulant cohesion. This weakened the driving forces for foulant attachment and compaction, resulting in a thinner and looser fouling layer. Nutrient behavior was highly selective during coagulation-UF process. Nitrogen and potassium were largely preserved in the liquid phase, whereas phosphorus exhibited over 99% apparent concentration decrease under the optimized conditions, resulting in an overall nutrient concentration decrease of approximately 12%. Extended 24-h UF and downstream nanofiltration (NF) experiments further supported the improved fouling mitigation benefits of optimized coagulation. These results provided a mechanistic insight and a practical strategy for fouling-controlled BS pretreatment toward subsequent water reuse and nutrient management.

works.title: Techno-Economic Assessment of Membrane Distillation for Green Hydrogen Production in Australia
institutions: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
works.abstract: As global momentum builds toward decarbonisation, green hydrogen has emerged as a key pillar in Australia’s transition to a net-zero emissions future. However, the freshwater demands of large-scale electrolysis poses a significant social hurdle, particularly in a nation facing acute water scarcity. The SeaHydrogen approach, developed in the Netherlands, offers a potential solution by using waste heat from the electrolysis process to desalinate seawater via membrane distillation, enabling hydrogen production without drawing on limited freshwater supplies. This paper investigates the techno-economic feasibility of using membrane distillation as the desalination method for green hydrogen production, when compared to conventional reverse osmosis. The Arrowsmith Hydrogen Project in Western Australia was used as a case study to link the investigation to real world applications. Hydrogen electrolysis requires significant volumes of purified water, posing challenges in water-scarce regions such as regional Australia. Eight scenarios were modelled using brackish aquifer and seawater sources to evaluate capital expenditure, operational expenditure, levelised cost of water, and net present value for both desalination technologies. Results showed that membrane distillation achieved lower levelised cost of water values than reverse osmosis across all configurations (with reductions in cost between 15–37% for the cases considered). This was primarily due to its ability to utilise low-grade waste heat from electrolysers, substantially reducing energy demand and operational expenditure. Aquifer-sourced membrane distillation emerged as the most economically viable configuration. Integrated membrane distillation also presents other potential benefits, including lower energy intensity, reduced-liquid discharge, improved waste-heat recovery, and the option to produce a limited volume of surplus distilled water, either for on-site use or to supplement small local communities. The findings highlight membrane distillation as a promising alternative to reverse osmosis for sustainable hydrogen production, consistently delivering water for lower cost for the Arrowsmith site. Moreover the analysis shows that both methods can be used to generate excess potable water at prices that are competitive with existing water supplies.

works.title: Redox-Programmed Bipolar Membranes from Electronically Wired Ion-Insertion Hosts for Selective Ion Transport
works.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
institutions: the University of Texas at Austin , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Selective ion separation is critical for resource recovery, water purification, and electrochemical energy technologies, yet it remains difficult to combine high selectivity, high flux, and simultaneous transmembrane uptake and release in a single-membrane architecture. Conventional polymer membranes are scalable but often lack molecular specificity. Redox-active ion-insertion materials provide lattice- and redox-defined ion selectivity, but their transport requires electronic charge compensation, limiting their use as single-stage transport membranes. Here, we establish electronically wired ion insertion hosts as active electrochemical membranes for redox-programmed ion separation. Li+-insertion particles are connected into a composite electronic–ionic conductor (CEIC), transforming a battery-type host into a membrane that stores, relays, and releases Li+ through spatially coupled redox reactions. Li+ transport is dominated by Li1–xMn2O4-mediated insertion/deinsertion, with a minor contribution from direct ionic transport through the porous membrane. Under an applied driving potential, bipolar electrochemistry couples Li+ insertion at the brine side interface with Li+ release at the recovery side interface, producing directional transmembrane transport. A LiMn2O4-based CEIC selectively transports Li+ from Na+-rich brine; integration with a Li+-selective polymer layer further suppresses nonselective ion transport and increases the Li+/Na+ separation factor to ∼2000. Spatially resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy reveals a lithiation gradient across the membrane, providing direct structural evidence of redox-coupled transmembrane transport. Replacement of LiMn2O4 with LiFePO4 further shows that modularity extends to the insertion host itself such that membrane selectivity can be programmed by the choice of insertion chemistry. This work shows that inorganic insertion chemistry can program membrane selectivity beyond the polymer design.

works.title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
institutions: East China University of Science and Technology
works.abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and simulations show that steric confinement, dehydration penalties, and electrostatic interactions cooperatively raise migration barriers for multivalent ions in confined channels. The membranes achieve comprehensive mono/multivalent discrimination across both cationic and anionic systems. In multistage electrodialysis, they enable stage-amplified lithium enrichment from high-Mg brines with stable long-term operation and downstream recovery of crystalline Li 2 CO 3 . They also facilitate high-purity NaCl enrichment from simulated seawater. Overall, this platform offers a durable and energy-efficient route to selective resource recovery from complex aqueous streams.

works.title: Switchable Electroosmotic Delivery via Capillary Shrunken Reduced Graphene Oxide Membrane
works.abstract: Abstract A capillary-force-assisted reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membrane is developed for electrically controlled electroosmotic flow (EOF). By combining capillary drying with subsequent freeze-drying, structural shrinkage is used to continuously control the pore size and channel density of the membrane. The resulting membrane shows enhanced EOF together with switchable transport behavior enabled by electrical parameter regulation. Under the optimized 20 h capillary drying condition, the membrane exhibits an EOF intensity of about 1.15 μL min−1 cm−2 and enables symmetric four-mode electrical switching of EOF direction and intensity through independent regulation of driving current and membrane-bias polarity. This switchable EOF is further translated into switchable molecular delivery, allowing reversible regulation of glucose and FITC-dextran (MW: 10 kDa) transport between opposite directions; in the transport-favorable direction, the transported amounts are 3.23 and 5.06× higher, respectively, than those in the opposite direction. Together, these results provide a practical route for flexible electroosmotic systems requiring electrically switchable and reversible molecular transport.

works.title: Hierarchical Structured Electrospun Zein/ <scp>PLA</scp> / <scp>SiO</scp> <sub>2</sub> Composite Fibrous Membrane for Oil–Water Separation
institutions: Key Laboratory of Functional Fibers and Intelligent Textiles Shaoxing Institute of Technology Shaoxing Zhejiang China
Zhejiang Sci‐Tech University Hangzhou Zhejiang China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological materials have been widely applied in achieving wastewater purification and the construction of a sustainable society. In this work, a sustainable and eco‐friendly biomass fiber membrane was developed for oil–water separation. Based on zein as the primary material, the Zein/PLA/SiO 2 composite fibrous membrane with hierarchical structures comprising microscale groove‐shaped, nanoscale rod‐shaped, and microscale ribbon‐shaped was designed through composite electrospinning technology. The multiscale morphological structure, thermal stability, wettability, mechanical properties, and oil–water separation performance of the designed composite fibrous membrane were systematically investigated. We found that the synergistic effect of the hierarchical fiber structure endows the fibrous membrane with excellent mechanical properties, tunable superwettability, and remarkable adsorption capacity for various oils. Specifically, tensile stress of the fibrous membrane was significantly increased from 0.4 to 1.94 MPa, and the membrane exhibited a high adsorption capacity of up to 41.8 g/g. Moreover, it achieved a high emulsion separation efficiency of over 99% with the flux of 2638 L/(m 2 h), and maintained stable separation performance even after 30 cycles, demonstrating excellent reusability and long‐term stability. The further investigation into the structure–property relationship provides theoretical guidance for designing and fabricating novel, rapidly biodegradable, high‐efficiency oil–water separation fibrous membranes.

works.title: Preparation of Membrane Evaporators and Solar Interfacial Water Evaporation Performance Study
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane evaporators are widely used in solar interfacial water evaporation due to their low cost and convenient construction. However, they generally suffer from issues such as low evaporation rate, poor light absorption and temperature rise capacity, and weak salt resistance during evaporation in seawater. To address these issues, this study conducted ultrasonic treatment on membranes from medical absorbent cotton (AC) using ethanol as the medium for the evaporator. The membranes were coated with C and Fe elements using the impregnation metho and enriched with Ti elements using the in situ growth method. Then, the evaporators containing different elements were tested for photothermal water evaporation, surface temperature rise capacity under illumination, and salt resistance for seawater desalination. The results showed that different elements affect the weight loss curve, evaporation rate, and evaporation efficiency of the samples. The addition of Fe element on the basis of a C element coating can optimize the evaporation capacity of the sample, achieving an evaporation rate of 1.44 kg·m–2 under simulated 1 sun pure water conditions. The incorporation of Ti element effectively enhances the salt resistance of the membrane.

works.title: Engineering flexible Fe-BTCA@GO nanocomposite to enhance the antifouling and separation performance of PES ultrafiltration membranes
works.abstract: Flexible metal-organic frameworks (FL-MOFs) have emerged as promising nanofillers for advanced mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs), owing to their framework flexibility, high surface area and tunable pore architecture. The adaptive framework enables dynamic transport pathways that can enhance membrane permselectivity. However, these MOFs remain largely unexplored. FL-MOFs lacks clear molecular cut-off due to unregulated gate-opening effect, to address this issue MOF may be decorated with another material such as graphene oxide (GO). Herein, flexible (FL) paraffinic polycarboxylate MOF, namely iron-1,2,3,4 butanetetracarboxylic acid (Fe-BTCA), and GO composite were synthesised using solvothermal method. GO was introduced to enhance crystallinity and regulate framework flexibility yielding a novel Fe-BTCA@GO composite. The synthesised nanofillers were incorporated into polyethersulfone (PES) matrix through blending method to fabricate ultrafiltration (UF) membranes using non-solvent induced phase separation (NIPS) technique and evaluated their performance using dead-end filtration cell at 150 kPa. The incorporation of Fe-BTCA@GO significantly enhanced membrane hydrophilicity reducing water contact angle (WCA) from 77° (pristine PES) to as low as 48.7 o (Fe-BTCA@GO/PES membrane), bovine serum albumin (BSA) rejection improved from 87.5% (pristine PES membrane) up to 99.5% (Fe-BTCA@GO/PES). Whilst pure water flux (PWF), surface roughness (Ra), and flux recovery ratio ( FRR ) were also improved. These improvements are attributed to the nonbonding oxygenated functional groups (FGs) of Fe-BTCA and Fe-BTCA@GO, which enhanced membrane hydrophilicity, influenced rapid solvent-non-solvent exchange during phase inversion, promoted membrane porosity and reduced BSA adsorption. Overall, FL-MOF-incorporated MMMs demonstrate strong potential as high-performance UF membranes for protein separation and water purification.

works.title: Explicit Solvent Effects on Ion Selectivity and Membrane Potential of Charged Spherical Liposomes: A Classical Density-Functional Theory Investigation
works.abstract: Abstract In this work, we use classical density-functional theory (CDFT) to study ion selectivity and membrane potential in cationic and anionic spherical liposomes. The influence of surface charge, electrolyte concentration, cavity size, and solvent structure on these properties has been systematically studied. The liposomes are modeled as charged spherical vesicles with phospholipid bilayer membranes having cationic/anionic surface charges. To demonstrate solvent-mediated electrostatic effects, two complementary solvent descriptions are considered: the restricted primitive model (RPM), where the solvent is treated as a dielectric continuum, and the solvent-restricted primitive model (SRPM), where solvent molecules are explicitly represented as neutral hard spheres. Ion selectivity (χi) and membrane potential (ψMP) are systematically evaluated for liposomes in equilibrium with binary AB and CB2 electrolyte mixtures over a broad range of surface charge densities, electrolyte concentrations, and cavity sizes. Ion selectivity is improved by the surface charge, while the increasing electrolyte concentration reduces ion selectivity due to stronger electrostatic screening and enhanced ion–ion correlations, which modify ionic distributions within the liposome cavity. The selectivity is generally decreased with the increase of cavity sizes. Also, the predicted selectivity parameter by SRPM is smaller than that of RPM. The nonlinear behaviors for membrane potentials with charge inversion are observed under the situation of highly concentrated electrolytes. In contrast to the continuum-based RPM, the explicit solvent SRPM captures reduced magnitudes of membrane potentials correctly and describes charge inversion better by including solvent-packing and excluded-volume effects. These results give new insights into the solvent-mediated electrostatic interactions in confined lipid systems and provide a theoretical basis to understand the ion selectivity properties in charged liposomes.

works.title: Assessment of Heavy Metal Concentrations and Water Quality Parameters in Hemodialysis Water in Kirkuk, Iraq
works.journal: Science Forum (Journal of Pure and Applied Sciences)
works.abstract: Objective: To assess physicochemical parameters and selected trace/heavy metals in water before and after the reverse osmosis (RO) treatment system at the main dialysis center in Kirkuk, Iraq, and to compare the results with WHO reference values and applicable AAMI/ANSI/ISO requirements. Methods: Water was sampled at the RO inlet (In) and outlet (Out) at two-week intervals from the beginning of April to mid-May 2024. Samples were collected in 0.5-L polyethylene bottles and stored at approximately 8 °C until analysis. pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), electrical conductivity (EC), Na, K, Ca, Mg, and selected trace metals were measured using pH/TDS/EC meters, flame photometry, flame atomic absorption spectrometry, and ICP-OES. Results: pH decreased from 7.60 ± 0.0493 to 6.50 ± 0.0950. TDS decreased from 688.3 ± 1.528 to 6.00 ± 0.800 mg/L, and EC from 1459 ± 2.646 to 13.00 ± 1.00 µS/cm (P < 0.0001). Na remained below its applicable limit. K decreased from 9.439 ± 0.1063 to 4.053 ± 0.02292 mg/L (P = 0.0002). Ca and Mg decreased to 39.08 ± 0.02235 and 21.70 ± 0.1865 mg/L, respectively, but remained above their applicable limits (P < 0.0001). Zn, Pb, and Cd decreased after RO but remained above their respective limits; Cr was 0.0200 ± 0.0006 mg/L at the inlet (P = 0.004) and was not detected after RO at the reported analytical level. Fe remained detectable at 0.1044 ± 0.0001 mg/L before RO and 0.09550 ± 0.0002 mg/L after RO. Al, Be, Ba, As, Ag, Sb, Se, Tl, Co, Ni, Mn, and Cu were not detected at the reported analytical level. Conclusion: RO treatment substantially reduced several measured parameters but did not achieve chemical compliance for Ca, Mg, Zn, Pb, and Cd. The findings support routine monitoring and systematic evaluation of pretreatment, membrane condition, storage, and distribution components.

works.title: Janus Ag Nanoskin‐Armored Polyimide Bilayer Separator Enables Efficient Li‐Nucleation Regulation for Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Battery
institutions: Hebei University of Science and Technology
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Uncontrolled lithium (Li) dendrite growth has been regarded as the most critical obstacle for the widespread adoption of Li metal batteries (LMBs), stemming from the preferential nucleation of Li ions (Li + ) at low‐energy‐barrier sites that trigger heterogeneous deposition. Therefore, it is pivotal yet significantly challenging to effectively control Li nucleation and deposition in LMBs. Here, we engineer a Janus Ag nanoskin‐armored polyimide (Ag@PI/PI) bilayer separator by in situ growth Ag nanoparticles on the surface of PI nanofiber and integrating a high‐strength PI nanofiber membrane as the dorsal substrate. Specifically, the Ag nanoskin acts as a three‐dimensional lithiophilic host to seize Li and induce sequential Li nucleation, thereby preventing Li dendrite formation. As a result, the Ag@PI/PI‐Li||Cu cell exhibits a low overpotential of 31.0 mV, high Coulombic efficiency of 98.9%, and prolonged Sand's time of 26.3 h. Significantly, the Ag@PI/PI separator delivers a high Li + transference number (0.70) and exceptional cycling stability (1600 h) in a Li||Li cell. Moreover, the Ag@PI/PI‐based Li||NCM523 cell achieves a remarkable specific capacity of 108.32 mAh g −1 at 5 C while retaining a satisfying capacity retention of 88.7% at 1 C. These results underscore the viability of this universal and efficient Ag nanoskin‐armored strategy for high‐security LMBs applications.

works.title: Wireless Electrochemical Palladium Membrane Reactor
institutions: Institute of Inorganic Chemistry University of Bonn Bonn Germany
Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry California State University Bakersfield California USA
works.abstract: Electrochemical palladium membrane reactors traditionally rely on direct cathodic polarization of the palladium membrane to drive hydrogen permeation. This work introduces the wireless electrochemical palladium membrane reactor (wPMR), a design that utilizes bipolar electrochemistry to actuate hydrogen transport without direct electrical connections to the membrane. By redefining the palladium membrane as an “ajar” bipolar electrode, we demonstrate that it functions similarly to a diode, requiring a voltage threshold to initiate selective hydrogen transport along an induced external electric field. As a proof‐of‐concept, we integrated the wPMR with lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction, successfully synthesizing ammonia using hydrogen atoms derived directly from water. Unlike conventional systems that suffer from structural deformation due to lattice expansion, the wPMR maintains membrane integrity by avoiding the lattice‐expanded β‐PdH. Through isotope labeling and operando monitoring, we confirm the synchronous operation of four Faradaic reactions within this reaction geometry. The wPMR thus emerges as a high‐voltage electrosynthetic platform capable of directly delivering hydrogen from water to organic reactions.

works.title: Thirsty clean energy: localized water stress and hydro-ecological tradeoffs in green hydrogen expansion
works.journal: Critical Insights in Environmental Science and Technology
works.abstract: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologically fragile landscapes. This review critically examines the localized hydro-ecological tradeoffs of mega-scale electrolysis across arid export corridors in Australia, Chile, and North Africa. Moving beyond theoretical stoichiometry, the analysis deconstructs the true operational water footprint of commercial electrolysis and evaluates cascading secondary risks, including marine ecotoxicity from desalination brine, fossil aquifer depletion, and spatial ecosystem fragmentation. Prevailing sustainability frameworks are critiqued for their fatal overreliance on carbon-centric metrics, which systematically externalize ecological carrying capacities and socio-economic water justice, risking a new paradigm of green extractivism. Finally, the review outlines fact-based technological and regulatory horizons—including direct seawater splitting, circular wastewater integration, and planetary-boundary-informed zoning—necessary to decouple the clean energy transition from localized hydrological collapse.

works.title: Capillary Gel Electrophoresis Separation of dsDNA Molecules Using Tetrahydroxyborate Stabilized Hydroxyethyl Cellulose – Polyvinylpyrrolidone Physical Copolymer
works.abstract: Abstract The advent of nucleic-acid–based therapeutics has revived the need to develop efficient capillary gel electrophoresis methods for their rapid, high-resolution analysis. In this paper, we introduce a dual-network hydrogel-based physical copolymer, utilizing the excellent sieving properties of hydroxyethyl cellulose with interpenetrating polyvinylpyrrolidone, which also sufficiently suppresses electroosmotic flow. Boric acid in the background electrolyte served as a cross-linker/stabilizer for the hydroxyethyl cellulose-based separation matrix via the formation of spiroborane bridges. The addition of glycerol significantly increased the resolution of separations. The excellent sieving power of the tetrahydroxyborate-stabilized HEC-PVP physical copolymer is demonstrated by the separation of dsDNA restriction fragments in a wide base pair range of 67 to 10 000, even capable of resolving identical chain length fragments. As a practical example, plasmid DNA integrity monitoring was demonstrated, facilitating the path toward a novel high-resolution separation matrix for gene therapy products in the biopharmaceuticals industry.

works.title: Removal of copper and lead ions by red mud-metakaolin based geopolymer microspheres: Insights into the efficient preparation and adsorption mechanisms
works.abstract: Abstract This study used red mud and metakaolin as the main raw material, with sodium silicate as the alkali activator. Red mud-metakaolin based geopolymer microspheres (RM-MGMs) with good sphericity and high mechanical strength are prepared via dispersion-suspension-solidification method. By investigating the adsorption performance of RM-MGMs calcined at different temperatures for Cu2+ and Pb2+, the uncalcined RM-MGMs exhibit excellent heavy metal cation adsorption due to their abundant surface hydroxyl groups and high ion exchange capacity. The optimal adsorption conditions for Cu2+/Pb2+ were adsorbent dosages of 1.5/0.3 g/L, pH of 5.3-5.6/5.0, respectively. Cu2+ adsorption reached equilibrium at 960 min. Pb2+ showed faster adsorption rate due to its smaller hydrated ionic radius and reached equilibrium at 60 min. Kinetic results indicated that the pseudo-second-order model better describes the adsorption process of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+. Adsorption isotherm models showed that increasing temperature favors the adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs. At 318 K, the adsorption capacities of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+ reach 0.86/1.43 mmol/g, respectively. In competitive experiments, the removal rates of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs both exceed 80%. RM-MGMs achieve adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ through synergistic mechanisms including ion exchange, electrostatic attraction and complexation.

works.title: Influence of Polymer Hydrophilicity on Solvent-Driven Rare-Earth Element Binding Thermodynamics and Heat Capacity Changes
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
works.abstract: Abstract Rare-earth elements (REEs: La–Lu, Y, Sc) are critical to modern technology; however, their acquisition, purification, and separation from each other can be challenging, and current methods are often environmentally damaging. Metal-binding polymers are a promising material class to improve these methods, but fundamental structure–property relationships have yet to be fully developed. Inspired by nature’s use of solvation- and conformation-driven effects to control metal-binding interactions, we hypothesized that modifying the molecular environment around the binding sites on metal-chelating polymers could offer a way to modify solvation structure and direct these interactions. Specifically, we hypothesized that increasing binding-site hydrophilicity would increase the enthalpic favorability of polymer–metal interactions, while maintaining the entropic driving force of metal-ion dehydration. To test this hypothesis, we synthesized a series of poly(amino acid acrylamides) with systematic changes in the hydrophilicity around the metal-binding sites, using a modular polymer approach to hold key polymer parameters constant. We then used isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) to measure the solution thermodynamics of polymer–REE binding. Binding by all polymers in this series was entropically driven─consistent with substantial solvent reorganization─but binding site hydrophilicity did not significantly affect binding thermodynamics due to enthalpy–entropy compensation. Interestingly, poly(glutamic acid acrylamide) displayed a distinct binding behavior, possibly driven by reduced solvent reorganization and larger conformational contributions. In general, lower hydrophilicity was associated with larger desolvation signatures, which could indicate that hydrophobic groups more effectively dehydrate the metal ion than hydrophilic groups. Together, these results demonstrate how polymer structure can modulate desolvation and control polymer-REE binding while also highlighting thermodynamic constraints that limit straightforward tuning of binding affinity, thus providing new insights for the design of materials for critical metal purification.

works.title: Effect of Confinement on Ion Transport in Polymer Electrolytes
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
institutions: Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences , , ,
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences , ,
China Academy of Safety Science and Technology , ,
SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing Co., Ltd. , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Understanding ion transport in polymer electrolytes is important for elucidating the molecular origins of transport limitations and opportunities in nanostructured solid polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate how cylindrical confinement regulates the structure and dynamics of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based electrolytes. Decreasing the nanotube diameter drives pronounced polymer chain segregation and reorganizes the spatial distribution of coordinating oxygen sites. This confinement-induced structural rearrangement markedly suppresses ion–segment codiffusion along short chain segments and inhibits interchain hopping, leading to a substantial decrease in Li+ mobility. However, upon decreasing nanotube diameter, Li+–EO coordination becomes stronger, which amplifies distinct cation–cation correlations; this competition between slowed ion mobility and strengthened ion–ion correlations gives rise to a nonmonotonic dependence of ionic conductivity on nanotube diameter. To disentangle geometric confinement from specific polymer electrolyte–wall interactions, we perform control simulations with hard walls, where the hard wall provides only steric exclusion; these results confirm that the nonmonotonic trend cannot be explained by geometric confinement alone and instead requires the inclusion of specific polymer electrolyte–wall interactions. Together, our results reveal the intricate coupling among confinement geometry, interfacial interactions, polymer organization, and ion transport, providing an atomistic basis for understanding ion transport in nanochannel-confined polymer electrolytes.
